We saw earlier that the rotation in the plane through an angle $\theta$ is given by the matrix: $$ \left[\begin{array}{rr} \cos\theta \amp -\sin\theta \\ \sin\theta \amp \cos\theta \\ \end{array}\right] $$ . We would like to find a similar expression for the matrix that represents the reflection across $L_\theta$, the line passing through the origin and making an angle of $\theta$ with the positive $x$-axis, as shown in [fig-ex-reflection-def].

The reflection across the line $L_\theta$.

To do this, notice that this reflection can be obtained by composing three separate transformations as shown in [fig-ex-reflection-compose]. Beginning with the vector $\xvec$, we apply the transformation $R$ to rotate by $-\theta$ and obtain $R(\xvec)$. Next, we apply $S$, a reflection in the horizontal axis, followed by $T$, a rotation by $\theta$. We see that $T(S(R(\xvec)))$ is the same as the reflection of $\xvec$ in the original line $L_\theta$.

Reflection in the line $L_\theta$ as a composition of three transformations.

Using this decomposition, show that the reflection in the line $L_\theta$ is described by the matrix $$ \left[\begin{array}{rr} \cos(2\theta) \amp \sin(2\theta) \\ \sin(2\theta) \amp -\cos(2\theta) \\ \end{array}\right] $$ . You will need to remember the trigonometric identities: $$ \begin{aligned} \cos(2\theta) \amp {}={} \cos^2\theta - \sin^2\theta \\ \sin(2\theta) \amp {}={} 2\sin\theta\cos\theta \\ \end{aligned} $$ .

Now that we have a matrix that describes the reflection in the line $L_\theta$, show that the composition of the reflection in the horizontal axis followed by the reflection in $L_\theta$ is a counterclockwise rotation by an angle $2\theta$. We saw some examples of this earlier in [ex-compose-reflections].
